newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Finance Minister S A M S Kibria said the government would carry out reforms in a "syncronised and coordinated" manner to avert distortions in the economy. Kibria said international donors at last week's consultation in Paris had endorsed the idea.

Asian Development Bank (ADB) is likely to finance a five-year $30 million project to reduce the poverty level of slum dwellers in Dhaka. At least five million of Dhaka city's 9.3 million population live below the poverty line, according to a government-ADB joint study.
Government officers have been asked to keep their telephone bills within limit. An official source said a circular had been issued in this regard to stop "misuse" of telephones at government offices.

The government was seriously considering a proposal for forming a "metropolitan government" for Dhaka city, said Local Government Minister Zillur Rahman. The proposal, put forward by the Dhaka City Corporation, said the city mayor would be the chief executive of the metropolitan government which would be answerable to the head of the government.

Power workers have threatened to resist the government's move to purchase electricity from neighbouring India and Nepal. Trade unionists of the state-run Power Development Board (PDB) said they had written letters to the authorities to rescind the plan for power purchase and instead try for foreign investment in electricity generation at home.
Opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has blamed the ruling Awami League for what she called impeding the flourishment of parliamentary democracy.

The government is working on a new banking policy articulating the responsibilities of commercial banks and development financial institutions. Finance Minister S A M S Kibria initiated consultations on Sunday with chairmen of the banks on the subject, official sources said.

Chittagong Export Processing Zone would be expanded further to house another 56 industrial units, Executive Chairman of the Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Authority said. -- Dhaka Newsroom 880-2-506363
